te: Ministry of Labour heard before the visit to Norway and Sweden
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Ministry of Labour to give information for the bilateral meeting and visit to the Kingdom of Norway and the Kingdom of Sweden (21–28 June 2025), such as Sweden's new rules on seasonal workers, the Department of Skill Development's online Thai massage and language courses, and the Department of Employment's 5 legal channels for working abroad
it: The bilateral meeting and visit to the Kingdom of Norway and the Kingdom of Sweden (21–28 June 2025)

te: Discussion topics for Norway and Sweden prepared
se: The meeting prepared for the bilateral meeting and visit to the Kingdom of Norway and the Kingdom of Sweden (21–28 June 2025), setting topics such as raising Thai massage to international standards, the problems of Thai workers abroad, skills development, supporting older persons who wish to work, and cooperation on wild berry pickers
it: The bilateral meeting and visit to the Kingdom of Norway and the Kingdom of Sweden (21–28 June 2025)

te: Study visit on workplace safety in Songkhla and Satun prepared
se: The meeting prepared a study visit on welfare, labour protection and occupational safety and health in Songkhla and Satun Provinces on 7–10 May 2025, and considered 4 letters of complaint asking for checks on establishments in Rayong and Chon Buri Provinces that allegedly employ foreign workers instead of Thai workers, which did not give the petitioner's address
it: Study visit to Songkhla and Satun Provinces (7–10 May 2025)
Complaints about employing foreign workers instead of Thai workers (4 letters)

te: Visit to Udon Thani, Nong Khai and Laos prepared, and a Labour Day statement
se: The meeting prepared a study visit and bilateral labour meeting in Udon Thani and Nong Khai Provinces and the Lao PDR on 25–27 April 2025, approved publishing the committee's statement on National Labour Day, 1 May 2025, and noted the results of the Ranong study visit, where 200 questionnaires were collected from workers and business operators
it: Study visit and bilateral meeting, Udon Thani and Nong Khai Provinces and the Lao PDR (25–27 April 2025)
Statement on National Labour Day, 1 May 2025
Progress of the subcommittees' work followed up

te: Information gathered on 2 employment petitions considered
se: The meeting noted the preliminary information gathered on a petition about a dispute between a former employee and an employer. Finding that a ruling is a matter for the courts and that the petitioner could not be contacted, it ended its consideration. It also considered a petition concerning an employer that announced dismissals without paying severance
it: Petition on a dispute between a former employee and an employer
Petition concerning dismissal without severance pay

te: Petition closed with observations, and a visit to Ranong prepared
se: The meeting noted the information gathered on a petition requesting information from state agencies and agreed to end its consideration, sending an observation that the benefits and procedures insured persons should know about be communicated more completely. It noted the schedule of a study visit to Ranong Province on 2–4 April 2025 to follow up help for Thai workers detained in Myanmar and the registration of foreign workers
it: Petition requesting information from state agencies
Schedule of the study visit to Ranong Province (2–4 April 2025)
Progress of the subcommittees' work followed up

te: Petition concerning a work accident considered
se: The meeting considered a petition concerning an employee injured at work. The checks found that the petitioner had received help from the employer and had used the full social security medical care entitlement, so the meeting ended its consideration and resolved that the petitioner be informed, with advice on renewing the work permit correctly
it: Petition asking for help after a work accident
Progress of the subcommittees' work followed up

te: Samut Sakhon study visit summarised, and petitions on foreign workers summarised
se: The meeting noted the report on the study visit to Samut Sakhon Province for use in the report on the study of the motion, and noted the summary table of 20 petitions on the effects of foreign workers, with the reasons for ending their consideration as proposed by the secretariat
it: Report on the study visit to Samut Sakhon Province
Summary table of 20 petitions on foreign workers
Progress of the subcommittees' work followed up

te: Visit to Ang Thong on the sustainability of the Social Security Fund prepared
se: The meeting noted the schedule of a study visit to Ang Thong Province on 12 March 2025, with a forum to hear views on ways to strengthen the sustainability of the Social Security Fund, followed up the work of its subcommittees, and considered approaches to setting old-age benefits for insured persons under sections 33 and 39
it: Schedule of the study visit to Ang Thong Province (12 March 2025)
Approaches to setting old-age benefits for insured persons under sections 33 and 39
Progress of the subcommittees' work followed up

te: Study visit on foreign workers in Samut Sakhon prepared
se: The meeting noted the schedule of a study visit to Samut Sakhon Province on 7 March 2025, to hear information from government agencies, the private sector and civil society and to meet workers at their workplaces, and followed up the work of its subcommittees
it: Schedule of the study visit to Samut Sakhon Province (7 March 2025)
Progress of the subcommittees' work followed up

te: Programme for sending Thai workers to Japan discussed
se: The meeting noted the criteria for sending Thai workers to train in Japan under the IM Japan programme, and agreed to study cooperation to create job opportunities for conscripts nearing the end of their service. It followed up the work of its subcommittees, such as the use of digital platforms in labour administration and the study visit to Ranong Province
it: Approaches to promoting work in Japan for Thai workers under the IM Japan programme
Progress of the subcommittees' work followed up

te: Business sector heard on employing migrant workers
se: The meeting heard information from representatives of the Thai Chamber of Commerce and Board of Trade of Thailand on employing migrant workers under the government-to-government memoranda of understanding (MOU) and problems with changing employers, for use in its study of the motion
it: Motion on approaches to solving the problems of foreign workers who entered the country illegally and of work in occupations prohibited to foreigners

te: Labour agencies heard on foreign workers, and a visit to Norway and Sweden planned
se: The meeting invited the Department of Employment, the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare and the Social Security Office to give information on measures for managing migrant workers under Cabinet resolutions, for its study of the motion. It noted the approach to the bilateral meeting in Norway and Sweden in June 2025 and considered the schedule of the study visit to Samut Sakhon Province
it: Motion on approaches to solving the problems of foreign workers who entered the country illegally and of work in occupations prohibited to foreigners
Approach to the bilateral meeting in Norway and Sweden
Schedule of the study visit to Samut Sakhon Province

te: Report on migrant workers noted, and a petition from Phuket fishers
se: The meeting noted the study reports on social security and the management of migrant workers, and on the management of workers of 4 nationalities. It agreed to invite the agencies concerned and to visit Samut Sakhon Province, and considered a petition from fishers in Phuket Province about the complicated and lengthy procedure for renewing the work permits of boat crews
it: Study report on the management of migrant workers
Petition from fishers in Phuket Province on renewing work permits

te: Senator who proposed the motion on foreign workers heard
se: The meeting invited Mr. Parinya Wongcherdkwan, the senator who proposed the motion, to explain the background of the problem. He explained that foreign workers are an important economic force, but there are issues of illegal entry and of work in reserved occupations, so Thailand must balance respect for human rights with law enforcement
it: Motion on approaches to solving the problems of foreign workers who entered the country illegally and of work in occupations prohibited to foreigners

te: Motion on foreign workers taken up for study, and Thai workers held hostage followed up
se: The meeting noted the key points of the motion on approaches to solving the problems of foreign workers who entered the country illegally and of work in occupations prohibited to foreigners, proposed by Mr. Parinya Wongcherdkwan, senator, and others, and approved a study plan for preparing a report to the Senate. It also noted a request for help in following up and assisting Thai workers held hostage as a result of unrest abroad
it: Motion on approaches to solving the problems of foreign workers who entered the country illegally and of work in occupations prohibited to foreigners
Request to follow up and assist Thai workers held hostage
